# Story 37 — FE-07: Reports, Dashboards and the Customer Portal UI (Story: 484)

## Prerequisites

- Story 36 completed (`.squad/plans/frontend/36-story-*-483.md` — administration surfaces). This story reuses the same client conventions established there: generated Orval clients under `frontend/src/api/generated/`, hand-written `wire.ts` adapters per feature, `AsyncBoundary` + `shell/states/*` for loading/error/empty.
- Read `.squad/gaps/36-483.md` before starting. It documents the standing pattern for this codebase: **backend endpoints are frequently missing, mis-wired, or return a different shape than the OpenAPI spec suggests**. Sections 1, 3, 4, 8–12 of that file are concrete precedents. Any backend defect you find in reporting/portal during this story must be recorded the same way in a new `.squad/gaps/37-484.md` — **do not** silently patch backend code from a frontend story.
- Backend reporting and portal domains already exist (`app/Domains/Reporting/`, `app/Domains/Portal/`). No backend work is planned here.
- Coordinate before changing `frontend/src/api/generated/**` — that tree is generated by `frontend/orval.config.ts` from `docs/api/openapi.yaml`. Never hand-edit generated files; regenerate or wrap.

---

## Story Goal

Deliver two distinct surfaces on the existing React app:

1. **Internal reporting surface** — a reports section with **one shared filter bar** used by every report, report result tables whose figures are traceable back to the ticket detail they came from, and an export flow producing CSV / Excel / PDF.
2. **Management dashboard** — a single screen summarising operational health, rendered strictly from what the backend returns for the caller's scope (no client-side aggregation across scopes).
3. **Customer Portal** — a **separate application surface** with its own authentication, its own layout and branding, its own route tree, and no reachable internal functionality. A signed-in customer can submit, track, reply to and rate a request and browse published help content. A guest can track exactly one request via their link without an account.

**Explicitly not in scope:**

- Any change under `app/`, `routes/`, `database/` — this is a frontend story. Backend defects get logged as gaps.
- Report scheduling UI (`report-schedules` CRUD, wired at `routes/api.php:347`) — list only if trivial, otherwise defer.
- Live chat widget and web-form public rendering (separate public surfaces, covered by their own stories).
- Re-deriving SLA numbers on the client. `frontend/src/__tests__/no-sla-recalculation.test.ts` enforces this; keep it passing.

## Product rules (from story)

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| One filter bar | **All** reports share a single filter component. Available controls per report are driven by the report definition returned from `GET reports`, not by a per-report bespoke bar. |
| Figures are traceable | Every drill-down figure links to the ticket (or ticket list, pre-filtered) it was derived from. A number with no path back to its source is a defect. |
| Dashboard respects scope | The dashboard renders the scoped payload the API returns. No client-side scope selection beyond filters the API accepts. |
| Export formats | CSV, Excel (XLSX) and PDF, all three offered. Arabic correctness in PDF is server-rendered; the UI must not attempt client-side PDF generation. |
| Portal is separate | Its own auth, own layout, own branding, own route tree, own API client instance. Shared code is limited to the generic HTTP layer, i18n and primitive UI. |
| Portal capability set | Submit request, track requests, reply on a request, rate a resolved request, browse published help content. Nothing else. |
| Guest tracking | One request, via link, no account. The guest sees that request only. |
| No internal leakage | Manipulating an identifier in a portal URL must never surface internal data. The portal renders whatever the API authorises and nothing more; a 403/404 renders `ForbiddenState`/`NotFoundState`, never a partial internal view. |

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Reporting API layer

**Create file: `frontend/src/features/reports/types.ts`**

Domain types only — no generated types leaking into components. Model after `frontend/src/features/tickets/types.ts`.

```ts
export type ReportId = string;

export interface ReportFilterDescriptor {
  key: string;              // matches a parameter accepted by ReportQueryRequest
  type: 'dateRange' | 'select' | 'multiSelect' | 'boolean';
  required: boolean;
  options?: Array<{ value: string; label: string }>;
}

export interface ReportDefinition {
  id: ReportId;
  title: string;            // bilingual-aware; resolve via the same helper as features/tickets/utils/bilingual.ts
  filters: ReportFilterDescriptor[];
  columns: Array<{ key: string; label: string; numeric: boolean }>;
}

export interface ReportResult {
  columns: Array<{ key: string; label: string; numeric: boolean }>;
  rows: Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
  meta?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export type ExportFormat = 'csv' | 'xlsx' | 'pdf';
```

**Shape these fields against the real payloads.** Read `app/Domains/Reporting/Http/Resources/ReportDefinitionResource.php` and `ReportResultResource.php` and `app/Domains/Reporting/Services/Definitions/ReportResult.php` first, and make the TypeScript match them exactly. If the resource does not expose filter descriptors, that is a **gap** — record it and fall back to deriving the filter set from `ReportQueryRequest.php`'s accepted parameters for the interim, with a `TODO(gap-484)` comment naming the missing field.

**Create file: `frontend/src/features/reports/api/wire.ts`**

- `fetchReportDefinitions()` → wraps `getReports` (`frontend/src/api/generated/reporting/reporting.ts:31`), unwraps the collection envelope via the existing helper in `frontend/src/api/http/envelope.ts`, returns `ReportDefinition[]`.
- `fetchReport(id, filters)` → wraps `getReport` (same file, line 93). Serialise filters exactly as `ReportQueryRequest.php` expects; **drop** any key the definition did not declare.
- `requestExport(id, format, filters)` → `POST reports/{report}/export`. This route is behind the **`idempotency` middleware** (`routes/api.php:344`) — send an idempotency key header using whatever mechanism `frontend/src/api/http/mutator.ts` already provides; grep the mutator for `Idempotency` before writing this and match the existing convention exactly (see `app/Http/Middleware/EnforceIdempotency.php` for the header name).
- `fetchExportStatus(exportId)` → only if the backend exposes a read route. Grep `routes/api.php` for `exports` first. If no such route exists, the export UI must not poll — record the gap and treat the POST response as terminal.

**Create file: `frontend/src/features/reports/api/errorCodes.ts`** — map the reporting error codes to i18n keys, mirroring `frontend/src/features/admin/api/errorCodes.ts`. Cover at minimum: unknown report, range too large, unsupported export format, export not ready, export expired, export too large. Take the exact code strings from `app/Support/Http/Errors/ErrorCode.php` and confirm each has an entry in `lang/en/errors.php` **and** `lang/ar/errors.php`.

### 2 — Shared report filter bar

**Create file: `frontend/src/features/reports/filters/ReportFilterBar.tsx`**

- **One component, used by every report and by the dashboard.** It takes `filters: ReportFilterDescriptor[]` and a controlled value object, and renders only the controls the descriptor list declares.
- Filter state lives in the URL query string so a report view is shareable and back/forward works. Use the router primitives already used in `frontend/src/features/tickets/list/useTicketListQuery.ts` (read it — it is the established filter-state pattern) rather than inventing a second approach.
- Required filters that are empty **block** the fetch and render inline validation from i18n; do not send a request that `ReportQueryRequest.php` will reject.
- Date-range control must respect the range ceiling enforced by `ReportRangeTooLargeException` — read the limit from config if the API exposes it, otherwise surface the server error rather than guessing a client-side maximum.

**Create file: `frontend/src/features/reports/filters/useReportFilters.ts`** — reads/writes the query string, normalises defaults from the definition, exposes `{ values, setValue, reset, isComplete }`.

**Create file: `frontend/src/pages/reports/ReportsIndexPage.tsx`** — lists the report definitions from `fetchReportDefinitions()`. Wrap in `AsyncBoundary`; `EmptyState` when the list is empty; `ForbiddenState` on 403 (a user without the reporting permission must not see a blank grid).

**Create file: `frontend/src/pages/reports/ReportDetailPage.tsx`**

- Resolves `:reportId` from the route, finds its definition, renders `ReportFilterBar` above the result.
- Renders `ReportResultTable` (below). Numeric columns right-aligned in LTR and mirrored under RTL — the app already ships Arabic; verify direction handling against `frontend/src/i18n/LocaleProvider.tsx`.
- **Traceability:** each row that represents ticket-scoped data links through to the ticket list pre-filtered with the equivalent query, or to the ticket detail when the row is a single ticket. Reuse the existing ticket-list query-string keys from `frontend/src/features/tickets/list/useTicketListQuery.ts` so the destination filter genuinely reproduces the figure. If a report's rows carry no ticket identifier or filterable dimension, the drill-down is not buildable — **record that as a gap** rather than fabricating a link.
- Export control offering CSV, Excel and PDF, calling `requestExport`. On success show the async-export acknowledgement state; on `ReportExportTooLargeException` / range errors show the mapped localized message from `errorCodes.ts`.

**Create file: `frontend/src/features/reports/results/ReportResultTable.tsx`** — generic column-descriptor-driven table. No per-report table components.

**Create file: `frontend/src/features/reports/export/ExportMenu.tsx`** — the three formats, disabled while a request is in flight, with an explicit "your export is being prepared" message. **Do not** implement client-side CSV/PDF generation as a fallback; the Arabic PDF requirement is only satisfied by the server exporter (`app/Domains/Reporting/Services/Export/PdfReportExporter.php`).

## Backend Tasks

**No backend changes required.** Every reporting and portal endpoint this story consumes already exists in `routes/api.php` (lines 126–150 and 342–347) with controllers under `app/Domains/Portal/Http/Controllers/` and `app/Domains/Reporting/Http/Controllers/`.

If you discover a missing or broken endpoint — most likely candidates, based on the `.squad/gaps/36-483.md` precedent, are an absent export-status read route, missing filter descriptors on `ReportDefinitionResource`, and a missing portal attachment **upload** route — **do not fix it here**. Write it up in `.squad/gaps/37-484.md` using the section format of `.squad/gaps/36-483.md` (symptom, evidence with file:line, impact on the plan, suggested fix) and implement the frontend against the degraded contract with a `TODO(gap-484)` comment.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Report with required filters not yet chosen** — the page must render the filter bar and an instructional empty state, and must not fire a request `ReportQueryRequest.php` would 422. Enforced in `useReportFilters.ts` (`isComplete`) and gated in `ReportDetailPage.tsx`.
- **Date range exceeds the server ceiling** — backend raises the range-too-large error (`app/Domains/Reporting/Exceptions/ReportRangeTooLargeException.php`). Surface the mapped localized message inline on the filter bar, do not blow up the page.
- **Unknown report id in the URL** — `UnknownReportException` on the server; render `NotFoundState`, not an error boundary crash.
- **Export requested twice rapidly** — the route is idempotency-wrapped (`routes/api.php:344`, `app/Http/Middleware/EnforceIdempotency.php`). Reusing the same idempotency key must not create two exports; changing filters must produce a new key. Disable the export control while in flight.
- **Export too large / not ready / expired** — three distinct exceptions in `app/Domains/Reporting/Exceptions/`. Three distinct, localized user messages. An expired download link offers "request again", not a dead button.
- **Arabic PDF direction** — verified by inspecting the downloaded artefact, not by a client assertion. If the PDF renders Arabic reversed or LTR, that is a **server** defect in `PdfReportExporter.php` / `resources/views/reports/export.blade.php` → log as a gap; do not attempt a client-side workaround.
- **Manager with narrow scope** — the dashboard payload is already scoped (`ReportScopeResolver.php`). Empty metric groups render as zero-value cards with an explanatory empty state, not as a broken layout.
- **User without the reporting permission** — nav entry hidden by `useVisibleNavigation.ts`, and direct URL entry renders `ForbiddenState` via `RequirePermission`. Both paths must be covered; hiding the nav alone is insufficient.
- **Portal user manipulates a ticket id in the URL** — API returns 403/404 under the `auth:portal` guard and `PortalTicketScope` (`app/Domains/Portal/Services/Visibility/PortalTicketScope.php`). The page renders the portal `ForbiddenState`/`NotFoundState` and **nothing else** — no partially populated header, no cached data from a previous ticket. Reset query state on route param change.
- **Portal user manipulates an attachment id** — `PortalAttachmentGuard` (`app/Domains/Portal/Services/Visibility/PortalAttachmentGuard.php`) governs; frontend renders a denial state, never an inline broken image with a leaked filename.
- **Agent and customer signed in simultaneously in one browser** — distinct session storage keys (`frontend/src/auth/session.ts` vs `frontend/src/portal/auth/portalSession.ts`). Logging out of one must not log out the other, and neither client may send the other's credential.
- **Guest link visited twice, or after expiry** — expired grant renders the expiry state. A guest link must never grant access to a second request even if an identifier is edited.
- **Portal feedback submitted twice** — `TicketFeedbackAlreadySubmittedException`; the UI shows the existing rating read-only.
- **Unverified portal account attempts login** — `PortalAccountNotVerifiedException`; route the user into the verify flow rather than showing a generic auth failure.
- **Bot protection rejects registration** — `BotProtectionFailedException`; show a retry-able localized message, never a raw error code.
- **Unknown: export status polling.** It is not confirmed that a read route for `ReportExport` exists. Resolve this by grepping `routes/api.php` for the export controller **before** building any polling loop; if absent, the acknowledgement is terminal and the gap is logged.
- **Unknown: portal branding source.** No branding endpoint has been confirmed. Resolve or log; do not hardcode.

## Verification Steps

Confirm the exact script names first: `grep -A 12 '"scripts"' frontend/package.json`.

1. **Frontend type-checks:** from `frontend/`, run the TypeScript build (`npm run build`, or `npx tsc -b` if the build script is bundler-only). Zero errors.
2. **Frontend lints:** from `frontend/`, `npm run lint`. `frontend/eslint.config.js` is authoritative; zero errors, zero new warnings.
3. **Frontend tests:** from `frontend/`, `npx vitest run`. All tests pass, including the four existing guard tests and the new portal-isolation scan.
4. **Frontend runs:** from `frontend/`, `npm run dev`. Manually walk: `/reports` → pick a report → set filters → results render → drill-down lands on a ticket list whose count matches the figure → export each of csv/xlsx/pdf. Then the dashboard on one screen.
5. **Portal runs:** in the same dev server, visit `/portal`. Confirm the layout matches `docs/ui/customer-portal-reference.html` side by side. Register → verify → login → submit a request → see it in the list → reply → rate it → browse help. Then open a guest tracking link in a private window.
6. **Isolation check (manual):** while signed in to the portal, edit a ticket identifier in a `/portal/tickets/:id` URL to one you do not own. Expect a portal denial state and **no** internal data in the response body or the DOM. Repeat for an attachment identifier.
7. **Cross-session check (manual):** sign in as staff in one tab and as a portal customer in another. Confirm neither session is affected by the other's logout, and that the staff API rejects the portal credential (`portal.deny`, `routes/api.php:154`).
8. **RTL check:** switch the locale to Arabic on both surfaces. Layout mirrors, numeric report columns align correctly, portal matches the reference under RTL.
9. **Arabic PDF check:** download a PDF export with Arabic content and open it. Text must be shaped and right-to-left. A failure here is a backend gap, not a frontend fix.
10. **Backend regression:** from the repository root, `php artisan test --filter="Reporting|Portal"`. All green — this proves the contracts the UI is built on are intact.

## Migration / Rollback

- **No schema changes.** Rollback is a straight revert of the frontend commits.
- **New route surface:** `/portal/*` is additive and does not alter existing staff routes. If the portal branch must be pulled, remove the branch from `frontend/src/router.tsx` and delete `frontend/src/portal/**` and `frontend/src/pages/portal/**`; nothing under `frontend/src/features/**` or `frontend/src/shell/**` depends on them (the isolation test guarantees the dependency direction is one-way).
- **Half-applied risk:** the portal shipping with the staff auth stack partially reused. Guard against it by landing `frontend/src/__tests__/portal-isolation.test.ts` **first**, before the portal pages, so the boundary is enforced from the first commit rather than audited at the end.
- **i18n risk:** adding `reports.*` / `portal.*` keys to `en.json` without `ar.json` leaves Arabic users with raw keys. Add both in the same commit.
